items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: That day, I played with five different groups including a family group from England... The father is Ernie and he's a fine and I would say, underrated clarinetist in his own country.

ctx.x: After the ceremony, we went to the big potatoes storage plant where the festival always takes place. It was eleven in the morning, and we heard the choir of Luneray directed by Mrs Francoise Suplice, who also played organ. The choir was composed by about 40 people, and sang spirituals and many religious songs of the type one can only hear in a Negro baptist church. For that wonderful celebration of my 50 years of trumpet, I also played a number with the choral, which was inspired as much by having me to play with…

That day, I played with five different groups including a family group from England which had the mother player accordian, the father playing clarinet, the eldest son who was 15 at the time, played piano, a daughter, 11, was the singer, and it was really enjoyable to hear her singing 'I ain't gonna give nobody none of my jelly roll'. The youngest son plays trumpet and he was 9 years old. He did a good interpretation of Louis Armstrong, doing 'Sleepy time down South'. The name of the family is Tomasso. The father…

This 50 years of trumpet did not mean that I had been a professional musician that long, because it had taken me almost 3 years of learning the instrument and two more years before I joined an orchestra of any importance. But the word 50 years of trumpet playing spread and there were quite a number of celebrations, articles in jazz magazines, T.V. shows, etc., and my birthday which came at a time when I was relaxing at a friend's country home in Switzerland, was celebrated more so as a salute to the trumpet years…
